title: Computer Age Management Services Ltd - 543232 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: CAMS Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 18% YoY to a record INR183 crore, with margin up 270bps to 46.4% despite muted MF AUM growth.
summary.overview: Operating revenue grew 11.5% YoY to INR395 crore and EBITDA grew over 18% to INR183 crore, the highest ever, with PAT up 17%. MF revenue grew under 10% while non-MF revenue grew over 28%, led by Pay (up ~67-70%) and AIF (up ~25%), while KRA declined after the April 2026 pricing reset. Management said July AUM recovered strongly and expects FY27 blended revenue growth of about 13% and EBITDA growth of about 16%. Non-MF margin fell to about 13% in Q1 from over 17% last quarter, which management attributed mainly to the KRA dip.

financial_highlights.change: just under +15% YoY; market share about 67.2%

segments.name: Mutual fund (asset-based)
segments.commentary: MF revenue grew about 11% on asset-based revenue, with absolute MF revenue up under 10%; management sees no quarter-on-quarter yield decline. Equity AUM grew 17.6% and equity net sales and live SIP counts grew ahead of industry.

segments.name: Pay (payments)
segments.commentary: Grew just short of 70% YoY, driven mainly by credit card transactions after the PA licence; management said cards will be grown step by step given low margins.

segments.name: AIF / Alternatives
segments.commentary: AUM crossed INR3.2 lakh crore, grew mid-20s (about 25%), with 50 new mandates won in the quarter.

segments.name: KRA
segments.commentary: Revenue fell YoY after the April 2026 pricing reset (rates down about 29-30%); management expects recovery from Q2.

segments.name: SIF and GIFT City
segments.commentary: SIF: 11 unique SIFs launched, about INR12,000 crore accumulated and about INR1,000 crore net sales per month, nearly 50,000 investors. GIFT City retail: about INR750 crore AUM from first 10,000 investors.

segments.name: CAMS Repository, AA, pension
segments.commentary: Not yet EBITDA positive; management expects CAMSRep to turn EBITDA positive on a Q4 basis. Think Analytics is near breakeven.

guidance_outlook: FY27 blended non-MF revenue growth of about 20%, possibly 22-23%; MF revenue growth of at least 12%; blended revenue growth about 13% and EBITDA growth about 16%.
Non-MF margin expected to recover to about 17% for the year, 'close to 20%' by year-end, per management's varying comments.
Employee cost growth target about 5% YoY for FY27; total cost growth target below 10% per year for the next two to three years.
Enterprise headcount to fall about 5% in FY27; net employee cost benefit expected to be about 3-3.5% rather than 5%.
Operating margin expansion of about 1% a year, with possibility of 1.5%.
PAT margin expected to stay at about 30-31%; FY27 PAT growth about 31% if EBITDA growth is about 45%, per Ram Charan's answer.

On-prem capex about INR75 crore in the coming year, declining later; re-architecture total cost about INR500 crore, of which about INR290 crore capex, with about INR40 crore capitalised in Q1 and at least another INR80 crore in the rest of FY27.
Depreciation expected to rise, not fall, for the rest of FY27 by INR4-5 crore, due to re-architecture capitalisation.
capex_capacity: On-prem capex about INR75 crore in the coming year, falling in later years as cloud migration progresses.
Re-architecture project cost about INR500 crore, of which INR123 crore spent so far; about INR290 crore to be capex on a 10-year amortisation.
About INR40 crore re-architecture capitalised in Q1 FY27; at least INR80 crore more expected in the rest of FY27.
Transaction acceptance module of new platform going live Aug-Sep; full transaction acceptance concept by year-end. Four of eight transaction types live; all expected by November.
About 10% of gross payload converted to AI-based acceptance at maker level, to scale to 100% in 12 months.
demand_pricing: Market conditions muted in April-June; July materially better, AUM close to INR60 lakh crore but not yet there.
SIP collections held at just under INR60,000 crore in Q1; SIP collections and unique investor base grew faster than industry.

Yields: no quarter-on-quarter decline in Q1; compression from 4Q FY26 and 1Q FY26 is now in the base; residual compression for the next 3-4 quarters expected to be small. Historical 2.5-3% annual yield decline cited as likely.
KRA: pricing reset from 1 April 2026 cut rates about 29-30%; some fetch services that were free are now priced. Management says pricing is uniform across KRAs.
Mid-size AMC renewals: a couple concluded and two in discussion; impact on pricing expected to be very muted and already in Q1 pricing.
Non-asset MF revenue down YoY on lower NFO activity, the NSE arrangement winding down and application fees; QoQ also hit by MF Central and OPE.

qa_highlights.question: Expected AUM growth and yield compression behind the 13% blended revenue guidance, and downside risk (line dropped, not answered in full)
qa_highlights.answer: Question was cut off by a line drop before management responded; the outlook was not restated in that exchange.

qa_highlights.question: How many mid-size AMCs are up for renewal this year and is their pricing impact already in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A couple of mid-size AMC renewals concluded and two more are in discussion; the impact is expected to be very muted and is already in Q1 pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did KRA revenue fall when CDSL saw a much smaller hit from the same pricing reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Some fetch services that were free are now priced, applying equally to CAMS; the revenue mix differs (CAMS is about 70-75% MF, 25-30% non-MF including DP and broking). Management says pricing is uniform across KRAs and the Q1 impact was not large.

qa_highlights.question: Non-MF margin in Q1 and expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-MF margin was about 13% in Q1 versus about 17% plus last quarter, seen as a one-quarter KRA effect. Management expects about 17% for the year, and at least close to 20% by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How does SIF economics work for CAMS?
qa_highlights.answer: SIF schemes are priced at the same rates as equivalent MF schemes; set-up costs for the separate segregated schema (11 SIFs) are already in the base, and scale-up defrays them.

qa_highlights.question: Headcount reduction and employee cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Enterprise headcount is targeted to fall about 5% in FY27, with 2-3% already down; net employee cost benefit is expected at about 3-3.5% because AI and automation hires offset some exits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5% employee cost growth target medium-term, and what about margin expansion beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The 5% employee cost growth is an end-of-FY27 year-on-year target (about INR500 crore base, adding INR25-30 crore). Total cost growth is targeted below 10% a year for the next two to three years; margin expansion of about 1% a year, with a possibility of 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-asset MF revenue decline YoY despite transaction growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Most transactions are digital; only a subset of paper transactions is billed. The YoY drop was driven by lower NFO activity, the NSE arrangement winding down and application fees. QoQ was hit by MF Central and OPE.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are AI and automation gains, and what is the payments and yield outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said benefits from the new platform are incremental, with productivity gains over about 3-4 years; cloud and hardware cost inflation will offset some. Payments growth is mainly credit cards under the PA licence and will be scaled step by step; nothing one-time. Yield compression from 4Q FY26 and 1Q FY26 is in the base; residual compression over 3-4 quarters is expected to be small, with a historical 2.5-3% annual decline.

qa_highlights.question: Capex, capitalisation and depreciation outlook, and implied PAT growth?
qa_highlights.answer: On-prem capex about INR75 crore; re-architecture cost about INR500 crore, INR290 crore capex, with INR40 crore capitalised in Q1 and at least INR80 crore more in FY27. Depreciation to rise by INR4-5 crore for the rest of FY27. With EBITDA growth about 45%, PAT growth is about 31%; PAT margin expected at 30-31%.

qa_highlights.question: Non-MF EBITDA breakeven status by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Account aggregator, pension and CAMS Repository are not yet EBITDA positive; CAMSRep is expected to turn positive on a Q4 basis. Think Analytics is almost at breakeven. Account aggregator adoption faces a bottleneck, mainly on the fintech and lending side.

risks_watch: Recovery in KRA revenue from Q2 FY27 after the April 2026 pricing reset (rates down about 29-30%); Q1 non-MF margin fell to about 13%, and management needs it near 17-20% by year-end.
MF AUM reached about INR56 lakh crore but has not yet hit close to INR60 lakh crore; April-June was muted and July recovery must hold.
Employee cost growth target of about 5% and total cost growth below 10% a year for two to three years; cloud and hardware cost inflation could offset AI-driven savings.
Re-architecture: about INR80 crore more capitalisation in FY27, rising depreciation, and transaction acceptance modules going live Aug-Sep with all eight transaction types live by November.
Yield: residual compression for 3-4 quarters expected to be small, with a historical 2.5-3% annual decline; mid-size AMC renewals in discussion (two pending).
Payments growth is concentrated in low-margin credit cards, so margin dilution is a risk if the mix shifts further toward cards.
Management's comments on non-MF margin varied (about 17% versus close to 20%), and the 1% vs 1.5% margin expansion remains unconfirmed.
key_quotes: So on a blended basis, 11.2% MF revenue growth, 28% plus non -MF growth.
And there was nothing onetime. We've said this in the past, Abhijeet, that to build the book, we never take anything onetime and then drop it in the next quarter.
We are not doing it today because there's a risk in kind of just blindly doing it.
So, you should look at our headcount currently to be just shy of 8,300 for the company.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth levers (Pay, AIF, SIF, GIFT City, new AMC logos) and on cost discipline, but cautious and hedged on KRA recovery, yield outlook and margin targets, with several answers saying "let's watch it" or "we'll see by year-end". Management was defensive about the KRA pricing comparison with CDSL and declined to give revenue numbers for ConsentPro.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 blended revenue growth of about 13% and EBITDA growth of about 16%, with non-MF revenue growing 20%+ and July AUM recovering, but KRA pricing cuts of about 29-30% and a cut in non-MF margin guidance to about 17% temper the outlook; growth is mainly from pricing, digital and non-MF rather than new physical capacity, which is light (INR75 crore on-prem capex).
